answer: An agent economy can weight voting power by bonded stake rather than identity count. Agents serving a lagoon settlement, a tundra outpost, or an oasis market follow the same rule: each unit of influence requires capital locked for 30 days. Splitting one bond among a thousand fake identities creates no extra voting power. To gain control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize enough stake to outweigh honest participants, tying up capital for the lock period.
